phases.title: Survival
phases.goal: Handle greetings, introduce yourself, and manage basic needs with set phrases.
can: Pronounce Spanish reliably: the five pure vowels, rolled rr, silent h, and ñ
Use ser and estar in the present to say who and how you are
Conjugate regular -ar/-er/-ir verbs in the present tense
Count 0–100 and tell the time with son las... y media
Ask basic questions with qué, dónde, cuánto and cómo
Use masculine/feminine articles (el/la/un/una) with correct noun gender
phases.daily: 15 min vocabulary flashcards, 10 min pronunciation drills (vowels + rr), 5 min conjugating one regular verb aloud.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.goal: Talk about daily routines, likes, and plans in the present and near future.
can: Talk about the past with the preterite of regular verbs and key irregulars (fui, tuve, hice)
Use reflexive verbs like levantarse and llamarse with me/te/se
Express likes and dislikes with the gustar construction (me gusta/me gustan)
Form the near future with ir a + infinitive
Use estar + gerundio for actions happening right now
Master stem-changing verbs (e→ie, o→ue, e→i): quiero, puedo, pido
phases.daily: 15 min listening to slow Spanish audio, 10 min writing 3 sentences about your day, 10 min preterite conjugation practice.

phases.title: Core Structures
phases.goal: Narrate past events and connect ideas in longer, natural sentences.
can: Contrast the preterite and imperfect to narrate stories (jugaba cuando llegó)
Use direct and indirect object pronouns before the verb (lo veo, le hablo)
Combine two pronouns, turning le/les into se (se lo di)
Use the present perfect with haber + participle (he comido, has visto)
Distinguish por and para for cause vs. purpose
Give commands with the imperative, including irregulars (di, haz, ven)
phases.daily: 20 min graded reader, 10 min narrating a past event using preterite + imperfect, 5 min irregular participle review.

phases.title: Fluency
phases.goal: Express opinions, wishes and hypotheticals; understand native speech at normal speed.
can: Form and use the present subjunctive after querer que, ojalá and cuando
Use the conditional to be polite and to hypothesize (me gustaría, viajaría)
Build the imperfect subjunctive for si clauses (si tuviera, hablaría)
Handle relative clauses with que, quien, cuyo and lo que
Use comparatives and superlatives, including mejor, peor, mayor, menor
Understand and produce the passive and impersonal se (se habla español)
phases.daily: 25 min native podcast or series without subtitles, 15 min conversation exchange, 10 min journaling using subjunctive and conditional.

phases.title: Mastery
phases.goal: Communicate with near-native precision across formal and idiomatic registers.
can: Use compound and hypothetical tenses fluidly (pluscuamperfecto, futuro perfecto, condicional compuesto)
Build third-conditional sentences (si hubiera sabido, habría venido)
Switch registers between formal usted and colloquial tú/vosotros naturally
Deploy idioms and regional expressions appropriately (¡qué va!, vale, tener ganas de)
Recognize dialect differences (Spain vs. Latin America: vosotros, vos, ustedes, seseo)
Write structured, cohesive texts using advanced connectors (sin embargo, no obstante, por lo tanto)
phases.daily: 30 min reading literature or news, 20 min speaking on complex topics, 10 min noting new idioms and refining nuance.
